_readme: More places to eat for variety, researched Oct 2026 (Sonnet agent + spot checks). Coordinates estimated from addresses.

items.name: Kádár Étkezde
items.blurb: Legendary old-school canteen on Klauzál tér, back since autumn 2025. Főzelék, pörkölt and pancakes at near-communist prices, plus a proper Hungarian breakfast now.
items.tip: Főzelék with a fried egg or a pörkölt: about 1,650–2,500 HUF for a dish (£4–6). Daytime only. Half the tables book online, the rest are walk-in.

items.name: N28 Wine and Kitchen
items.blurb: Michelin Bib Gourmand Hungarian kitchen and wine bar a few minutes from the Airbnb. Open kitchen, almost all Hungarian wine and grown-up food without the silly prices.
items.tip: Daily Hungarian plates with a Hungarian red: about 9,000–13,000 HUF (£21–31) a head with wine. Book for Fri or Sat.

items.name: Bock Bisztró
items.blurb: Proper modern Hungarian cooking in the Corinthia hotel on the Nagykörút, with a big list of Villány reds from the Bock family. A sit-down dinner with a bit of class.
items.tip: Veal cheek pörkölt and a Villány red: about 9,000–14,000 HUF (£21–33) a head with wine. Book ahead for Fri and Sat.

items.name: Csirke Csibész
items.hours: Open until 05:00 Wed–Sat (opening time not confirmed)
items.blurb: Tiny 30-year-old corner joint doing a breaded chicken roll with Russian salad. Cheap, greasy and serving till 5am Wed to Sat. Textbook end-of-night fuel.
items.tip: Crispy chicken roll with Russian salad: roughly 1,500–2,500 HUF (£4–6). Small place, so expect a short wait when the bars kick out.

items.name: Pizza Me (Wesselényi utca)
items.hours: Reported open until 06:00 every night (2024 guide): check Google Maps
items.blurb: Italian-style pizza by the slice, a few minutes from the ruin bars and open until dawn. Point at a slice, eat it on the pavement, carry on.
items.tip: Two slices and a drink: about 1,800–3,000 HUF (£4–7). Expect a queue once the bars shut. Cash or card, no booking.

items.name: Szeráj
items.hours: Daily from 10:00 · closes about midnight–01:00 Sun–Thu and about 04:00–05:00 Fri–Sat (listings vary)
items.blurb: Turkish place on the Nagykörút that one guide calls the best eat-in or takeaway kebab in the city. Big menu, plenty of seats and hours that run deep into the night.
items.tip: Mixed kebab plate or a wrap with a drink: roughly 3,000–5,000 HUF (£7–12). Walk-ins fine. About 25 min walk or a tram ride away.

items.name: Deep Burger (Dob utca)
items.hours: Late hours reported, exact times not confirmed: check Google Maps
items.blurb: Small downtown burger chain that We Love Budapest tips for a post-party burger. The Dob utca branch sits right in the ruin-bar zone. Quick, greasy and cheap enough.
items.tip: Burger and chips with a drink: about 3,500–5,000 HUF (£8–12). Check Maps for current late hours before relying on it.

items.name: Hachi-Ko
items.blurb: New ramen and izakaya spot by Madách tér from the Hachi team, opened January 2026. Cold-brew dashi broths and small plates, and it stays open till midnight Fri and Sat.
items.tip: Ramen 4,380–5,480 HUF (£10–13), add a couple of small plates. Walk in early, or ask about booking.

items.name: 94' Konyha & Bar
items.blurb: Michelin Bib Gourmand Vietnamese kitchen: proper pho and a beef fried rice with XO sauce in a plain, friendly room. Top quality for not much money. About 25 min walk.
items.tip: Pho plus the 94' Gohan: roughly 5,000–8,000 HUF (£12–19) a head. Book for Fri and Sat nights.

items.name: Phở 18
items.blurb: Vietnamese on Ráday utca with big bowls of pho, plus pad thai and bao. Good value, friendly staff and a short stagger to the Ráday bars afterwards.
items.tip: Duck or beef pho: roughly 3,000–5,000 HUF (£7–12) a head. Soup is the hangover cure of choice. Walk-ins fine.

items.name: Bombay Budapest
items.blurb: Contemporary Indian near the Basilica with a strong vegetarian list and the usual hits. Reviews are mixed on service and speed, so go hungry and patient.
items.tip: Butter chicken, lamb curry and plenty of naan to share: about 6,000–9,000 HUF (£14–21) a head. Book Fri and Sat.

items.name: Arriba Taqueria (Teréz körút)
items.hours: Check Google Maps for opening times
items.blurb: Build-your-own tacos and burritos close to Oktogon. Not Mexico City, but quick, cheap and a good break from paprika. A local reviewer rated it the best taqueria they'd tried in town.
items.tip: Three tacos and a drink: about 3,500–5,000 HUF (£8–12). Order at the counter, no booking needed.

items.name: Forni di Napoli (Bazilika)
items.blurb: Award-winning Neapolitan pizza two minutes from the Basilica. Blistered wood-fired crust, a menu of around 30 pizzas, so even the fussy one in the group is sorted.
items.tip: Pizza plus a beer: about 4,500–7,000 HUF (£11–16) a head. Book for Fri and Sat evenings.

items.name: Hot Stone Steakhouse
items.hours: Lunch and dinner daily (exact hours not confirmed): check before booking
items.blurb: Cook your own steak on a lava stone heated to 400 degrees, steps from the Basilica. A bit of theatre and a different beast to Pampas.
items.tip: Priced by the gram: budget roughly 12,000–20,000 HUF (£28–47) a head with a drink. Book ahead for the weekend.

items.name: Bigfish Seafood Bistro
items.blurb: Budapest's go-to seafood bistro on Andrássy út, with sea fish brought in from the Budaörs market. Grilled fish, oysters and proper seafood plates, a short walk from the Airbnb.
items.tip: Grilled fish of the day with a starter: about 9,000–14,000 HUF (£21–33) a head. Book for weekend evenings.

items.name: Cirkusz Café
items.blurb: Big breakfast place on Dob utca, open from 7:30 every day. Full English, bagels, Benedicts and a pulled-pork omelette. Proper hangover armour.
items.tip: English breakfast and a coffee: about 4,500–6,500 HUF (£11–15). Busiest 10 to noon, so go early or expect a wait.

items.name: Goli
items.hours: Tue–Sat 12:00–22:30 · Sun closed · Mon closed per Michelin (OpenTable says open)
items.blurb: Middle Eastern cooking with a Michelin Bib Gourmand, near the Basilica. Mezze and grills built for sharing, and good value for the quality.
items.tip: Share a pile of mezze and grills: about 7,000–10,000 HUF (£16–24) a head. Book, especially Fri and Sat.

items.name: Time Out Market
items.address: Blaha Lujza tér 1 (Corvin Palace, 1st floor), 1085 Budapest
items.priceText: Mains about 4,000–6,000 HUF, a Dreher tank beer about 1,250–2,000 HUF, cocktails 3,000–4,000 HUF. No service charge since September 2026
items.hours: Daily 11:30–23:30 · kitchens stop serving at 22:00 · bars' last orders about 23:00
items.blurb: Food hall in the restored Corvin department store at Blaha. Eleven kitchens, from Michelin-pedigree Hungarian to burgers, pho and pizza, and three bars pouring tank Dreher, Hungarian wine and cocktails, all around long shared tables.
items.tip: Straight down the körút from the Airbnb. Everyone orders from a different kitchen and meets back at one table. Go in from the Blaha Lujza tér side and take the escalator up. Kitchens stop at 22:00, so eat first. Football goes on the big projector wall, and there are DJs on Thursday evenings.
items.history: Built in 1926 as the Budapesti Nagyáruház, then wrapped in aluminium panels as the Corvin department store in the 1960s. The original façade was restored as Corvin Palace, and Time Out Market opened on its first floor on 20 September 2025.

items.name: Hari Kebab
items.priceText: Hari Kebab pita about 3,200 HUF, plates from about 3,800 HUF on the delivery apps, a bit less in the shop
items.blurb: The name that comes up most for the best döner in Budapest: soft homemade pita, crispy veal or chicken off the spit and fresh veg. Colin Farrell's pick when he was filming here.
items.tip: Order the Hari Kebab, which comes with feta and caramelised onions. It shuts at 21:00, so this is a daytime or dinner feed, not a 3am one.

items.name: Piramis Kebab
items.priceText: About 2,000 HUF for a shawarma and a drink
items.blurb: Egyptian-run shawarma and falafel on the theatre street, with some of the best ratings of any kebab shop in the city. Big portions, proper sauces, halal.
items.tip: A shawarma in pita with everything on. Closed Sundays and shuts at 21:00. It's a couple of doors from Csirke Csibész.

items.name: Melissa Bisztró (Greek gyros)
items.blurb: Greek gyros pita with proper tzatziki in the party district, open till 5am. The original shop of the chain and a regular on after-party lists.
items.tip: You want no. 18, not the sit-down Melissa Greek Taverna further along at no. 31. Pita gyros with everything.

items.name: Istanbul Kebab (Akácfa utca)
items.hours: Daily from 08:00 till about 04:00 · to 05:00 Thu · to 05:30 Fri–Sat
items.blurb: The classic 4am döner and gyros stop between the ruin bars and Blaha. Not the finest meat in town, but it's open when nothing else is.
items.tip: Classic gyros with cabbage, onion and hot sauce. The latest-opening kebab in the app.

items.name: Istanbul Kebab & Grill
items.priceText: Cheap: a döner and tea for well under 3,000 HUF
items.hours: Daily from 08:00 · to 04:00 Thu–Sat, to midnight other nights (its own site also says 02:00 daily)
items.blurb: Top of Restaurant Guru's best-döner list for Budapest in 2026, a few streets from the Basilica. Good meat, big portions and free Turkish tea.
items.tip: Handy after the Basilica or a night in District V. Ask the price of extras like cheese before they go on.

items.name: Döner Master
items.priceText: Döner pita 1,850 HUF, tortilla wrap 2,200 HUF, the big Döner Master pita 3,500 HUF
items.hours: Mon–Thu 11:30–00:30 · Fri–Sat 11:30–02:30 · Sun 11:30–00:00 (delivery-app hours; one listing says 21:00, so check)
items.blurb: Turkish-style döner on the Nagykörút by Corvin-negyed: pita, wrap or a plate, with big portions of juicy meat and late opening at weekends.
items.tip: Tram 4 or 6 four stops south from the Király utca stop. The Döner Master pita is the big one.
